voice.text: The sun is going down. The sky is getting dark. [pause] Will the sun come back tomorrow? Tap your guess.
The sun comes up. [pause] The sun goes down. [pause] Then it comes up again! <emphasis>Day, night, day, night — again and again.</emphasis>
Seasons repeat too, always in the <emphasis>same order</emphasis>: [pause] spring, [pause] summer, [pause] fall, [pause] winter — then spring again! Around and around.
Weather changes every day. But we can <emphasis>write it down!</emphasis> [pause] Sun, sun, cloud, rain… look — a pattern! [pause] And remember: one rainy day does not change the season.
Build the season wheel, finish the patterns, and match the seasons. [pause] Tap the answer that comes next.
The wheel starts at spring. [pause] What season comes next?
After summer, what season comes next?
After fall, what season comes next?
After winter, the wheel goes around again! [pause] What comes next?
Day, night, day… [pause] What comes next?
Night, day, night… [pause] What comes next?
Spring, summer, fall… [pause] What season comes next?
Mittens on! Snow is falling. [pause] Which season is it?
Leaves turn orange and drift down. [pause] Which season is it?
Flowers bloom and baby birds hatch. [pause] Which season is it?
Yes! [pause] The wheel always turns the same way.
Yes! [pause] The pattern repeats.
Yes! [pause] Those clues match that season.
Not quite. [pause] Seasons never jump around. They always go in the same order, around the wheel.
Not quite. [pause] After day comes night, then day again. The sun always comes back.
Not quite. [pause] Look at the clues, and think which season shows them.
All patterns found! [pause] Now show what you know.
The sun goes down at night. What happens in the morning? [pause] The sun comes up again, [pause] or, the sun is gone forever?
What season comes after summer? [pause] Fall, [pause] winter, [pause] or spring?
What season comes after winter? [pause] Spring, [pause] or summer?
One hot, sunny day comes in spring. Did spring turn into summer? [pause] No — weather changes day to day and the season stays, [pause] or, yes — a hot day means it is summer now?
How can we find the weather pattern? [pause] Write the weather down every day, [pause] or, we can't — weather is just random?
<soft>You found nature's patterns!</soft> [pause] Well done.
Good try! Let's watch the patterns once more.
Lesson done! Start your weather journal today. Draw what the sky looks like, every day.
